title: Arceus · resources
description: The VM itself: whether CPU, memory, disk or network slows the agent down, and when.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: All cores, averaged over 5 min.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used, by what the kernel counts as available. There is no swap: past 100% processes are killed.

panels.title: Disk used, /
panels.description: Amber and red where the runner's health check warns (25% free) and stops new work (10% free).

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time the disk had requests in flight, over 5 min. Near 100% the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Waiting on I/O
panels.description: Share of time at least one task was stalled waiting for the disk (Linux pressure stall information).

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: 5-minute load average divided by the number of cores. Above 1, work queues for the CPU.

panels.title: OOM kills, 7 days
panels.description: Processes the kernel killed for lack of memory in the last week. Any is a reason to look.

panels.title: Up for
panels.description: Time since the VM booted. A short one explains a gap in the graphs.

panels.title: Agent
panels.description: When a task held the agent. The graphs below share its time axis; task starts and ends are also marked on every graph.

panels.title: CPU by kind of work
panels.description: User: programs (Claude, Codex, tests, the dev stack). Waiting on disk: idle CPU with I/O outstanding. Taken by the host: time the hypervisor gave to other VMs.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Cache is given back when programs need it; Available already counts it.

panels.title: Pressure: share of time work was stalled
panels.description: Linux pressure stall information: of all time, how much at least one task could not run for lack of that resource. The direct answer to which resource slows the agent down.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Runnable and disk-blocked tasks. Above the Cores line, work waits.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second. Clones, Docker images and test databases show up here.

panels.title: Disk operations
panels.description: Requests per second. Many small writes (git, package installs) load a disk more than their bytes suggest.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time the disk had requests in flight.

panels.title: Time per operation
panels.description: Average latency of one request. A rise without more operations means the disk (or the host's storage) is slow, not that we ask more of it.

panels.title: Disk queue
panels.description: Average number of requests queued or in service.

panels.title: Processes blocked on I/O
panels.description: Processes in uninterruptible sleep, almost always waiting for the disk.

panels.title: Growth, 7 days
panels.description: How much more disk is used than a week ago. Blank until there are 7 days of data.

panels.title: Free in 30 days
panels.description: Free space in 30 days if the last week's trend goes on. Red when it would run out. Blank until there are 7 days of data.

panels.title: Inodes used, /
panels.description: Files and folders, not bytes: node_modules and git objects can run out of these first.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: The VM's own interfaces: clones, pushes, model API calls, image pulls.

panels.title: Network errors and drops
panels.description: Packets per second. Errors should stay at zero: a steady line explains timeouts to GitLab, YouTrack or the model APIs. A low, flat drop rate is usually broadcast traffic nobody listens to; a jump during a task is not.

panels.title: Last full cleanup
panels.description: Since the last full pass that finished without errors. One runs at least daily, in the first free moment; amber past 26 h, red past 50 h.

panels.title: Last pass
panels.description: partial: some removals failed and are retried later (see the log). report: the pass only logs what it would remove (cleanup.mode: report, or the runner in observe).

panels.title: Not put down to a task
panels.description: Leftovers the last pass found but could not tie to a finished task, so it left them: the dev stack, a person's work, or something to add to cleanup.protect. `arceus-runner cleanup --last` lists them.

panels.title: Freed by the last pass
panels.description: Free disk space after the last acting pass minus before it.

panels.title: Cleanup
panels.description: What each pass removed, kept on a second look, failed to remove, or deferred, and why.
